title: Deity of Christ
definition: The deity of Christ is the doctrine that Jesus Christ is fully and eternally God.
summary: Jesus is not merely a prophet, teacher, or created being; He is fully and eternally God.
christFocus: This doctrine focuses directly on Jesus Christ as true God, worthy of worship, trust, obedience, and faith.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture presents Jesus Christ as fully God. He is the eternal Word who was with God and was God. He is not a created being who later became divine, nor merely a messenger sent by God. He shares the divine nature and reveals God perfectly.

The deity of Christ is shown through His names, works, worship, authority, sinlessness, and unity with the Father. He forgives sins, receives worship, rules creation, gives eternal life, and reveals the Father in a way no creature could.

If Jesus is truly God, then His words carry divine authority, His sacrifice has infinite worth, and His resurrection declares Him to be Lord. The Christian faith stands on the truth that the Savior is both able to save and worthy to be worshiped.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people are willing to admire Jesus while denying who He truly is. This doctrine matters because a lesser Jesus cannot save. If Christ is not fully God, His sacrifice cannot bear the full weight of redemption and His authority can be treated as optional.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Worship Jesus as Lord, not merely as an example. Trust His words, submit to His authority, and confess Him boldly as God the Son. Let His divine worth deepen your reverence, obedience, prayer, and hope.
